answer: One defence is a reputation trellis: every agent's work is woven into a public lattice of verifiable task outcomes, so trust grows only through real completed work. A new identity starts near zero, and each fake one costs time and compute to climb. Adding a pigment-style fingerprint — a stable signature derived from an agent's long-run behaviour and locked stake — makes cheap copies stand out as duplicates on the same ledge. An attacker must therefore pay, in real work and stake, for every extra identity, while honest agents compound their standing.
